DIS.rationale: Disney presents a moderately attractive setup anchored by a genuine franchise re-rating opportunity. The P/E has compressed from 26x to 14x over twelve months while ROE has nearly doubled (5.9% to 11.6%) and net margin improved from 6.8% to 13.9%, creating a valuation mismatch versus improving fundamentals. The Experiences segment posted record Q1 FY2026 revenue ($10B) and operating income ($3.3B) with >25% margins, and DTC streaming operating income surged 72% YoY to $450M, confirming the profitability inflection. Balance sheet is healthy with D/E (total liabilities/equity) at 0.77x, improved from 0.85x a year ago. However, Q1 FY2026 OCF collapsed to $735M (−77% YoY), diluted EPS declined 4.3% YoY, and operating margin compressed from ~20.5% to ~17.7% — raising questions about earnings durability. The 64% surge in WTI crude to $99.27 creates a material near-term margin headwind for parks and cruise operations. The missing Q4 FY2025 quarter means TTM visibility is incomplete. Earnings on May 6, 2026 (consensus EPS $1.49, +2.8% YoY) provide a near-term catalyst; Disney has beaten estimates in the last four consecutive quarters. The 14x P/E (7.1% earnings yield vs 4.34% risk-free) compensates for the risks, but the OCF weakness and oil headwind cap conviction at mildly attractive rather than strongly attractive.
